commercial_use_note: Every item in `items` carries either a publisher-stated public-domain position or a publisher-stated free licence. No item requires a paid licence. Two of the three legal bases carry conditions that are recorded per item and repeated in `constraints`.

legal_bases.label: California state work, public domain by operation of California law
legal_bases.applies_to: California Department of Water Resources stills and video
legal_bases.the_position: California state government works are NOT automatically public domain the way US federal works are. There is no federal-style statutory exclusion. The public-domain position rests on County of Santa Clara v. CFAC, which holds that a California public entity cannot enforce copyright in public records absent express statutory authorisation. DWR is not among the agencies California law authorises to claim copyright.
legal_bases.who_asserts_it: Wikimedia Commons, via Template:PD-CAGov. This is a community legal analysis applied per file, NOT a grant from DWR.
legal_bases.template_caveat_quoted: Wikimedia Commons makes no guarantee of the adequacy or validity of this information.
legal_bases.what_dwr_itself_asserts: Nothing helpful. https://water.ca.gov/Conditions-of-Use was opened in full: it contains Privacy, SECURITY and DISCLAIMER sections and the footer line 'Copyright © 2026 State of California'. It contains NO section headed Ownership, NO public-domain statement, and NO reuse grant. The nearest thing to a permission anywhere on DWR's own estate is https://water.ca.gov/Library describing its photo library: 'Our web-based photo library, Pixel, features a vast collection of images of California's natural landscapes, waterways, and other features of interest, available for free download.' That is a description of a download button, not a licence.
legal_bases.strength: GOOD BUT INFERRED. This is the honest characterisation. It is the same basis Wikipedia relies on for its entire Oroville Dam crisis article, and no counter-claim by DWR was found. It is not a written permission and should not be described as one.
legal_bases.sister_agency_note: The one California publisher that DOES assert the position in writing is Cal OES, whose Conditions of Use says in terms: 'In general, information presented on this web site, unless otherwise indicated, is considered in the public domain. It may be distributed or copied as permitted by law.' The identical clause appears on CHP's site. DWR's own site omits it. This inconsistency is the single weakest point in the whole rights picture and is why LB-1 is rated inferred rather than granted.

legal_bases.label: US federal government work, no copyright
legal_bases.applies_to: DVIDS (DoD) stills and video; NASA imagery; USGS imagery
legal_bases.quoted_dvids: DoW VI that are works of authorship prepared by U.S. Government employees as part of their official duties are not eligible for copyright protection in the United States.
legal_bases.quoted_dvids_use: DoW VI may be distributed, copied, and used, for non-commercial, personal use, as well as historical and newsworthy purposes or activities.
legal_bases.quoted_dvids_endorsement: The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.
legal_bases.quoted_dvids_caveat: some VI available on this publicly accessible website may be subject to copyright or other intellectual property rights owned by non-DoW parties.
legal_bases.quoted_nasa: NASA should be acknowledged as the source of the material. / NASA will not promote or endorse or appear to promote or endorse a commercial product, service or activity.
legal_bases.reading: The underlying legal fact is the absence of copyright. The DVIDS 'non-commercial, personal use' phrasing is a use-policy overlay, not a copyright restriction, and the same sentence expressly extends to 'historical and newsworthy purposes', which a documentary is. A monetised documentary must therefore carry the non-endorsement disclaimer and must not imply DoD or NASA endorsement. Recorded as a binding constraint, not a blocker.
legal_bases.strength: STRONG. Publisher states the position in writing, per asset, with a Public Domain badge on every asset page opened.
legal_bases.national_guard_wrinkle: Several items are California National Guard products. National Guard status (Title 32 vs Title 10) can complicate the 'federal employee' analysis. DVIDS nonetheless publishes them with the Public Domain badge and identical boilerplate. Where a purely federal alternative exists (509456 is 9th Reconnaissance Wing, an active-duty USAF unit; 3171587/3171592 are 60th Air Mobility Wing), prefer it for any hero placement.

legal_bases.label: Explicit free mark asserted by the holding institution
legal_bases.applies_to: California State Archives / California Revealed films on the Internet Archive
legal_bases.quoted: Public domain. No restrictions on use.
legal_bases.strength: STRONGEST of the three. An unambiguous written rights statement from the holding institution in a machine-readable metadata field. Its only weakness is subject matter: these are 1960s films, not the 2017 event.

items.beat: THE EVACUATION ON THE GROUND — the only state-published imagery of it that exists
items.publisher: California Senate Committee on Natural Resources and Water (document); California Department of Water Resources (author of the presentation)
items.presented_by: Bill Croyle, Acting Director, California Department of Water Resources
items.pdf_metadata: 34 pages; title 'PowerPoint Presentation'; author 'Eagan, Alicia'; creator 'Acrobat PDFMaker 11 for PowerPoint'; creationDate 2017-04-21
items.shows: A 34-slide chronological photo record, March 2016 to March 2017, one large photograph per slide. The evacuation-relevant slides, captions quoted verbatim from the file: slide 10 'February 12, 2017, approximately 5:20 p.m. | CHP officers review map' (804x452); slide 11 'February 12, 2017, approximately 6:45 p.m. | Residents receive updates on Oroville situation/evacuation' (809x455); slide 12 'February 12, 2017, 10:24 p.m. | Press conference regarding emergency spillway and evacuation' (1067x600); slide 13 'February 12, 2017 – CHP and local law enforcement aiding evacuations' (1183x664); slide 16 'February 14, 2017 | L to R: Butte County Sheriff Kory L. Honea, Cal Fire incident commander Kevin Lawson and DWR Acting Director Bill Croyle announce that the immediate evacuation order in Butte County has been reduced to an evacuation warning' (1200x675). Also slide 23 'February 20, 2017 | A handmade sign on Canyon Drive in Oroville gives thanks to emergency crews' (1200x780) and slide 29 'March 5, 2017 | Oroville residents make a special delivery of baked goods to show their support to the crews' (1200x793).
items.licence_quoted: NONE. The document contains no copyright notice, no photo credit, no courtesy line and no permission statement — a full-text scan of all 34 pages returned zero occurrences of 'copyright', '©', 'photo by', 'credit', 'courtesy' or 'all rights'.
items.rights_conflict: The underlying photographs are DWR's, which puts them under LB-1. But the document is hosted on a California Senate committee server, and the Legislature's own terms are materially more restrictive than the executive branch's. Quoted from https://www.assembly.ca.gov/privacy-and-conditions-use-policy: 'Some of the information presented on this web site may be protected by copyright. Permission to use that material must be obtained in advance from the California State Assembly, the California State Senate, or the Legislative Counsel Bureau, as applicable.' Which regime governs a DWR deck on a Senate server is genuinely unresolved.
items.rights_basis: review_required — DWR-authored photographs, legislature-hosted document, no statement in either the file or a governing terms page that settles it.
items.verification_detail: PDF retrieved and parsed locally with pymupdf. Page count, PDF metadata, every slide caption and every embedded image dimension were read from the file itself. The Assembly terms page was opened separately.
items.resolution_warning: The embedded images are 804-1200 px wide JPEG2000/JPEG slide graphics. Slide 10 at 804x452 is below 720p. These are presentation exports, not archive masters. They can carry a beat with treatment; they cannot carry a hero plate.
items.recommended_action: Before any use, ask DWR Public Affairs in writing for the originals of the slide 10-13 and 16 photographs and for a written statement of terms. They are DWR's own images and DWR advertises its photo library as free to download; a written reply would convert the strongest asset in question C from review_required to cleared, and would incidentally give LB-1 the written grant it currently lacks.

A.question: Are there at least a handful of clearable, genuinely usable Oroville 2017 clips — enough that the film's spine can show the real event rather than a reconstruction?
A.answer: YES for the dam. QUALIFIED for this film.
clips: PRESCREEN-V-002 — DWR, spillways 12 Feb 2017 (the day of the orders), 1080p, 2:01
PRESCREEN-V-003 — DVIDS/146AW, spillway and helicopter rock drops, 1080p, 8:55
PRESCREEN-V-004 — DVIDS/9RW, Beale AFB receives evacuees 12 Feb 2017, 1080p, 1:12
A.still_breakdown: 20 DWR stills on Commons individually confirmed public domain (2 opened as full file pages, 18 confirmed through the Commons API extmetadata endpoint), 1 NASA ISS still, 8 DVIDS federal stills opened individually. Two DVIDS sets of 18 and 13 are known to exist with their sizes stated on pages this session opened; only the 6 members opened individually are counted.
A.plus: 3 further California State Archives DWR films (1968 and undated, 22-41 min each, 720x540) under an explicit 'Public domain. No restrictions on use.' — historical, not 2017.
A.the_qualification: Roughly 15 minutes of clearable 1080p video exists, and all but 72 seconds of it is the DAM. This film is not about the dam. The premise says so itself: its own thumbnail_power justification retires the eroding-hillside image because 'it sells the dam, and this film is not about the dam.' What the film actually opens on — a woman walking into a supermarket, strangers shouting, a town emptying, a shelter at a fairground — has no clearable footage at all. So the spine CAN show the real event in the sense that the thing that caused the order is on camera at high resolution and free; it CANNOT show the event the film is about.

B.question: Does that satisfy the real_footage bonus as the planning OS defines it?
B.bonus_definition_quoted: {"key": "real_footage", "points": 5, "question": "Genuine bodycam, CCTV, dashcam, court or news footage is available and clearable."}
B.reasoning_literal: The bonus names five categories. Taken one at a time against what was actually verified: BODYCAM — none found, no source published any. CCTV — none found. DASHCAM — none found. COURT footage — none; Oroville Dam Cases No. C090941 is a California civil appeal with no video record, and the 2023 companion C093600 likewise. NEWS footage — this one exists and is the closest call, and it fails on the second half of the test rather than the first: the KRON, KTVU, KNTV, MSNBC and Fox recordings of 12-15 February 2017 are real and were located on the Internet Archive TV News Archive, but every one returns licenceurl = null, the TV News Archive grants research access rather than a reuse licence, and the two press evacuation stills that surfaced (Appeal-Democrat, KQED) are third-party copyright which Cal OES's own Conditions of Use expressly directs you to clear with the owner. Available, not clearable. On the literal reading the bonus fails on all five limbs.
B.reasoning_generous: Read generously as 'genuine footage of the real event is available and clearable', the answer is yes for the dam and no for the film. Fourteen of the fifteen clearable minutes show concrete, water and helicopters. The bonus's five named categories share a common shape — a recording system or a press camera that captured the event as it happened to people. Agency B-roll of infrastructure is a different thing, and it is the thing this topic has.
B.why_not_award_anyway: Awarding would move 85 to 90 and flip RESERVE to PRODUCTION. A bonus that decides a band must not be awarded on a stretch, which is the standard the scorer already applied to recognizable_institution in this same premise. The instruction on marginality was explicit: if marginal, say marginal and do not award. This is marginal in the generous reading and a clean fail in the literal one, so it is not awarded under either.
B.what_would_change_it: One of two things, both cheap. (1) The Beale AFB evacuee stills at beale.af.mil and nellis.af.mil open and turn out to be federal public-domain photographs of evacuees and cots — that would put real people, on the real day, in the film, from a free federal source. (2) A written reply from DWR Public Affairs releasing the slide 10-13 originals at archive resolution — CHP officers with a map, CHP and local law enforcement aiding evacuations, residents being briefed at 6:45pm on 12 February. Either would move this from marginal to arguable. Neither has happened, so the score stands at 85.
B.what_this_finding_IS_worth: The bonus is not awarded, but the producibility picture improved materially and that is a separate axis. The v002 producibility block records dam_spillway_reservoir as '29 clips, of which roughly half are genuine dams and none is Oroville.' That is no longer the position: there are now 4 verified Oroville video clips and 26 verified Oroville stills, most at 2000-7000px, all free. The AMBER gate reasoning should be revisited on its own terms — not by adjusting the score.

C.question: Do any of these sources cover the Silver Dollar Fairgrounds shelter or the evacuation itself — the two beats the shelf cannot dress (emergency_shelter = 1 clip; supermarket = 29 candidates of uncertain quality)?

what_was_checked: Cal OES Flickr (calemaphotos) — albums 2009 to 2025, no Oroville or February 2017 album.

Cal OES 2017 Oroville After Action Report (36pp) — contains no photographs at all beyond cover logos, and never names Silver Dollar Fairgrounds. It does confirm 'Fairgrounds in surrounding unaffected areas served as the primary location for shelters' and names Chico.
Cal OES five-year retrospective — its two shelter images are credited 'Red Cross Photo' and 'The Washington Post Photo'.

American Red Cross official Flickr (NSID 7172404@N06) — zero public photos, zero albums; an in-account search for 'oroville' returned 'Oops! There are no matches for your search in this user's photos.'
redcross.org — 403 on every path including its terms page; Red Cross terms are therefore unestablished and must be assumed restrictive.

Wikimedia Commons — the category holds 43 files and a MediaSearch for 'Oroville evacuation 2017' returns 2 results, neither an evacuation scene. Wikipedia's own Oroville Dam crisis article uses 20 images and not one shows an evacuation or a shelter.
Butte, Yuba and Sutter counties — no published imagery; Butte asserts all rights reserved, Yuba's terms are non-commercial only, Sutter returned 403 throughout.
silver_dollar_fairgrounds.conclusion: There is no government-published photograph or video of the Silver Dollar Fairgrounds shelter. The free-licence visual record of this entire event is engineering, not people. This beat must be budgeted as a labelled reconstruction under HC-6, exactly as the v002 producibility block already warned ('budget the shelter sequence as a non-archive solution at the premise stage, not at assembly'). This prescreen confirms that warning was right and closes the question.

what_exists: PRESCREEN-V-004 — DVIDS 509456, 72 seconds, 1080p, federal public domain: Beale AFB receiving Oroville evacuees on 12 February 2017. This is the only verified MOVING footage of the people the order moved. It is at an air base, not in Oroville.

PRESCREEN-S-009 slides 10, 11, 12, 13, 16 — the Croyle deck: CHP officers reviewing a map at 5:20pm, residents receiving updates at 6:45pm, the 10:24pm press conference, CHP and local law enforcement aiding evacuations, and the 14 February announcement reducing the order. All on 12-14 February 2017. Rights are review_required and resolution is 804-1200px.

PRESCREEN-S-006 — DVIDS 3169147 and 3169156, 5568x3712, federal public domain: inside the Cal OES State Operations Center on 15 February. Not the evacuation, but the room the orders came out of, which for THIS film may be worth more.
the_evacuation_itself.what_does_not_exist_free: Highway traffic, gas-station queues, an emptying town, a supermarket. The gridlock frames exist and are Appeal-Democrat and KQED — press, licensable for money, not free.

the_supermarket_opening_beat.answer: NOTHING, from any source, at any price that was checked.
the_supermarket_opening_beat.conclusion: The opening beat was always going to be a reconstruction and this prescreen changes nothing about that. HC-6 already governs it: labelled on screen, disclosed on YouTube, no real-person likeness, and thumbnail variant A is already written with exactly that constraint. The v002 staging plan's instruction to eyeball the 29-clip supermarket sub-register by hand before commissioning anything still stands and is untouched by this work.

NASA item: credit NASA and the ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility, Johnson Space Center, photo ID ISS050-E-52024. Do not imply NASA endorsement.

DWR/Commons items: attribution is not required by the licence tag, but credit 'California Department of Water Resources' anyway. LB-1 is an inferred position, not a written grant, and a visible credit is the cheapest form of good faith.
California State Archives films: no restrictions stated; credit the California State Archives / California Revealed as a courtesy.
PRESCREEN-S-009 (Croyle deck) is review_required, not cleared. Do not place it in a cut until DWR Public Affairs replies in writing or the images are located at DWR-hosted archive resolution.
NEVER repeat the DoD caption phrase 'in the aftermath of a dam failure near Oroville' — no dam failure occurred (see PRESCREEN-S-008 ACCURACY_WARNING).

No AI-generated image or motion may be presented as an authentic record of the 2017 crisis (HC-6). Everything in `items` is a genuine record and must be kept visually distinguishable from the reconstructions.
HC-1 still binds: Oroville Dam Cases No. C090941 is unpublished and must never be called precedent.
HC-3 still binds: no JCCP 4974 employee names anywhere. Nothing in this prescreen touches them.
